summary: Returned for the 2020 program, which ran fully remote and invited back only experienced teachers.
context: Breakthrough places fellows as teachers for middle school students. The 2020 program ran entirely over Zoom, and only teachers who had already done a summer were invited back to it.
actions: Taught daily lessons to two sections of 6th–8th grade students over Zoom.
Led the physical education program, remotely.

outcomes.claim: Invited back to a program that only took teachers who had already taught a summer.
Taught two sections daily through the program's first fully remote summer.

summary: Youngest teacher on a team of 65 at Breakthrough's flagship program, on the UT Austin campus, a 60-hour week teaching 8th grade history.
context: The 2019 program ran on the main campus of the University of Texas and is Breakthrough's flagship for middle schoolers. The fellowship is a full teaching load, not an assistantship: fellows write their own lessons and carry pastoral responsibility for named students.
actions: Designed lesson plans and taught two sections of 8th grade history.
Supervised lunch and conducted parent conferences.
Served as advisor to four students.
Spoke at my old high school about the program that autumn, and recruited students for future summers.

outcomes.claim: Was the youngest teacher on a team of 65.
Carried a 60-hour week across teaching, PE, supervision and advising.
Wrote and taught two sections of 8th grade history, rather than assisting someone else's course.
Advised four students directly and ran their parent conferences.
Went back to my old high school to speak about the program and recruit the next intake, so its pipeline did not rest only on staff.

image.alt: Speaking at a lectern in front of a seated audience, with a Breakthrough Central Texas slide projected on screen behind.
image.caption: Speaking about Breakthrough and recruiting for the next summer, October 2019.

summary: Nine weeks of sea turtle conservation across two sites on the Costa Rican coast, where the main defense against poaching was simply being there.
context: Poaching on that coast was a real and known problem, and the countermeasure was mostly bodies: people on the beach, visibly, so that anyone who came for the eggs would find it occupied. Volunteers rotated between two conservation sites, ASVO and Cirenas, in stretches.
actions: Walked night patrols along the beach, hours at a stretch in the dark.
Sat staged hatchery watches overnight, checking the fenced-off nests when the rotation came around.
Slept out on the sand on the other nights, presence being the whole point rather than any task.
Worked the unglamorous end of conservation between turtle shifts: a river cleanup near Cirenas, painting trash bins, sorting recycling.
Studied Spanish each morning before the day's work.

outcomes.claim: Kept two conservation sites visibly occupied overnight for nine weeks, a deterrent that works by presence rather than enforcement.
Rotated through both program sites, ASVO and Cirenas, across patrol, hatchery watch and site maintenance.
